profiles.meeting_scenario: At a university press, the legal team is holding a design review of the rights-clearance and publication-notice plan for a new critical edition of Otto Jespersen's Negation in English and other languages. The edition republishes Jespersen's original text, adds a newly commissioned scholarly introduction, re-typesets all linguistic examples into modern numbered format, and supplies Leipzig-style glosses for non-English examples. The agenda is to review whether the current clearance memo, contributor paperwork, and copyright-page language are sufficient for printer release and global distribution through the press's North American and UK channels. The expected outcome is a decision on whether the legal package is ready for sign-off as designed, or whether specific modifications are needed before production proceeds.

members.name: Dana Feld
members.expertise: Copyright, publishing law, cross-border rights, scholarly fair use analysis
members.background: Dana has spent twelve years advising academic publishers on reprints, critical editions, and permissions strategy, with particular experience in public-domain works that include newly created editorial apparatus.
members.private_state: Dana wants to approve the package without reopening the whole project timeline, but is quietly concerned that the press may be treating the added glosses and introduction as legally routine when they create a different rights profile from the original public-domain text.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says the book is a 'public domain text,' they mean only Jespersen's underlying original work, not the newly added introduction, glosses, numbering, and editorial apparatus.
Any reference to the 'examples' in the clearance file includes the examples exactly as they will appear in the new edition, including fresh gloss lines and editorial normalization.
A design review can conclude the project is 'ready for sign-off' once legal risk has been analyzed well enough for printer release, even if some clerical follow-ups remain.
If the project has reached formal legal review, the contributor agreement for the new introduction and editorial work has already been fully executed unless someone explicitly says otherwise.

members.name: Lewis Grant
members.expertise: Author agreements, permissions workflows, production contracting, rights metadata
members.background: Lewis manages contract administration for humanities titles and has overseen many republications of older scholarly works, where the main operational task is usually documenting public-domain status and inserting standard contributor language.
members.private_state: Lewis wants the review to validate that the project can move to production this week, and he is quietly trying to avoid adding new permissions tasks that would delay catalog copy and printer scheduling.
hidden_assumptions: Calling the project a 'public domain edition' effectively means the volume is clear to publish as a whole, with the new scholarly material handled through normal contributor paperwork rather than as a separate clearance question.

When the team discusses the 'examples,' they are mainly talking about the quotations inherited from Jespersen's source text, not the new formatting, glosses, or editorial presentation layered onto them.
'Ready for sign-off' means the permissions and paperwork workflow is substantively complete, with notices drafted and any needed outreach already launched.
For internal review purposes, a negotiated contributor agreement is practically equivalent to an executed one; signature timing can be cleaned up after approval.
If no one has raised territory-specific concerns, the standard global sales path for a public-domain reissue can be assumed.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'public domain text'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the project is a 'public domain text' or 'public domain edition.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means only Jespersen's original underlying text is in the public domain; the new introduction, glosses, example numbering, and editorial additions still require separate rights analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the volume is effectively publishable as a public-domain reissue, with the added scholarly material treated as routine ancillary matter already covered by normal contributor handling.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In academic publishing, 'public domain' is often used as shorthand for the commercial status of the whole project, so both hear a familiar phrase and assume the same level of legal granularity.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss checking or clearing the 'examples.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking about the final examples as printed in the new edition, including Leipzig-style glosses, normalized numbering, and any examples reproduced again in the introduction.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking mainly about the historical examples already contained in Jespersen's original book and listed in the source-text review spreadsheet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because the word 'examples' is perfectly natural in a linguistics book discussion, neither notices that one is referencing source quotations while the other is referencing the newly edited presentation of those materials.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about whether the package is 'ready for sign-off.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the legal review is sufficiently complete to authorize printer release, even if a few administrative items like updated metadata or filing final PDFs happen afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means all operational prerequisites are already in place, including finalized notices, launched permissions outreach if needed, and no missing contributor paperwork.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a routine milestone rather than a substantive standard, so each imports their own departmental threshold without treating it as something that needs explicit definition.

misalignment_points.topic: Assumed status of the new introduction agreement
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the introduction' as though its legal status is already settled.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the commissioned introduction and related editorial apparatus are already covered by a fully signed contributor agreement, because that is normally true before final legal review.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the unsigned but negotiated contributor agreement is sufficient for this stage and that execution can happen after sign-off without affecting today's review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither sees the status of the introduction agreement as today's main topic; each presumes business affairs has already handled it in the ordinary way, so the missing shared premise stays invisible.

For me, if the legal analysis is solid enough for printer release, the package can be ready for sign-off even if a few administrative cleanups happen afterward. I am also assuming, unless told otherwise, that the contributor agreement for the introduction and editorial work is already fully signed.
